messages.content: What does temperature change when a language model generates text?

Temperature changes how sharply the model samples from its next-token probabilities: lower values favor higher-probability tokens more strongly, while higher values make lower-probability alternatives more likely. Are you asking because you want more predictable output, or because you want to explore more varied generations?

messages.content: Why keep a validation set separate from the training set?

Because training performance alone cannot tell you how well the model handles data it did not optimize on. A separate validation set gives you an independent signal for choices such as checkpoint selection or hyperparameter tuning. Are you mainly using it to compare checkpoints, or to decide when training should stop?

Then consistency matters more than volume at first: keep the validation data and evaluation procedure fixed so checkpoint differences are interpretable. If two checkpoints have similar validation loss, what other behavior would you want to compare before choosing between them?
